Procedural
Programming
Part 2: External Modules
Programs can be separated into
separate files to increase readability
and maintainability.

Creating External Programs
As programs grow, keeping all code in one file can make
them harder to read and maintain.
External modules allow related functions and classes to
be moved into separate files.
The main program can then focus on the overall flow of
the program while supporting code is kept elsewhere.
This also makes useful code easier to reuse in other
programs.

Creating External Modules

The module file can then
be imported into another
Python program.

Documentation for External Modules
External modules should include clear documentation
so another programmer can understand how to use
them without reading all of the code.
Docstrings can describe what a module, function, or
class does, what parameters it expects, and what values
it returns.
Good documentation is especially important when a
module is designed to be reused by other programs.
